items.text: Amirhossein Mirasmaeili said a possible agreement between Saudi Arabia and the UAE could form a more effective military coalition in Yemen. He added that past disagreements benefited the Houthis and strengthening ground forces is important. Possible US involvement could increase military pressure on the Houthis.

Sara Bazoubandi said the US and the Islamic Republic currently have more willingness to reach an agreement, but significant disagreements remain. Washington aims to secure the Strait of Hormuz and end the Islamic Republic's nuclear program. The Trump administration has temporarily eased Russian oil restrictions to control fuel prices.

Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of War, said Iran must choose between abandoning its nuclear ambitions and reaching an agreement or facing US military action. He accused Iran of building a large missile arsenal alongside its nuclear program. Hegseth also mentioned Iran's financial support for Hezbollah and the Houthis.

Benjamin Netanyahu compared the Islamic Republic to cancer and said if the Iranian regime is not eliminated, it will return. He mentioned the possibility of renewed military action against Iran and accused the Islamic Republic of trying to influence Israeli elections. These statements were made in an interview with the i24 News network.

Donald Trump emphasized that Washington will not allow the Islamic Republic to rebuild its missile capabilities. The US Secretary of Defense announced the army's readiness for any conflict. Meanwhile, Tehran speaks of readiness for dialogue and tries to use regional developments as leverage in potential negotiations.

The Ilam Province Intelligence Department announced the arrest of 11 citizens in Malekshahi. These individuals were arrested for their alleged involvement in the December 2025 protests. The news was reported by Harana News Agency.

A worker died due to lack of safety and poor working conditions after falling from a height in Shahab Industrial Town, Qom. The inspector of the Supreme Association of Construction Workers' Unions announced the incident. Concerns have been raised about the safety and training conditions of workers.

Emiliano Martinez, Chelsea and Argentina goalkeeper, was injured after a severe collision with Jarrod Branthwaite. His head, neck, and back tests showed good results and he is conscious. Dibu has a jawbone injury and will undergo surgery.

On Saturday, October 17, hundreds of thousands protested in France against inflation and declining public services. Clashes occurred between police and protesters in cities like Paris and Lille, with some stores looted. Authorities reported 272 arrests nationwide.

Benjamin Netanyahu reiterated his commitment to overthrowing the Islamic Republic. He described this goal as an unfinished mission that must be completed. Netanyahu considered the Islamic Republic a threat to Israel that must be overthrown.

The German Foreign Ministry stated it will respond to Tehran's actions. This stance came after two individuals linked to the Quds Force were sentenced to 13 years in prison. Details of possible measures have not yet been announced.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said that Iranian officials claim Israel killed Ebrahim Raisi. He added that Israel largely determines or changes senior officials in Iran. He also said Israel changes the names of Tehran's streets, and the city council only installs the new signs.

Morad Veysi stated that subsidies were deposited for 11 million people with an additional 400,000 tomans. Initially, the payment was planned for 44 million people but was gradually reduced to about 10 million. He said the government is reneging on subsidy payments.

The Guardian reported that the UAE and Saudi Arabia have agreed to resume military cooperation against the Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic. The UAE will resume financial aid to Yemeni government forces, and Saudi Arabia will provide air support. This agreement indicates a reduction in the deep disagreements between Riyadh and Abu Dhabi over Yemen's future.

Meysam Mehrani said Washington's focus on Iran's nuclear issue without addressing missile programs and regional influence cannot resolve disputes. He warned that a phased agreement might allow Iran to rebuild its military capabilities. Mehrani added that continued naval blockade and economic pressure would benefit the US and harm Iran.

During the "Capital Operation" exercise in Norway, rented Chinese-made vehicles recorded video footage. The Norwegian army confirmed the recording but there is uncertainty about data sharing. Norway has imposed local security restrictions on these vehicles.

On Saturday, October 16, various cities in France witnessed widespread protests against rising living costs and declining public services, which in some areas led to violence and arson. Between 550,000 and 800,000 people participated in the protests, and about 400 were arrested. Government officials blamed the violence on the far left and promised to prosecute those responsible.

Armed groups in Iraq face financial difficulties due to US sanctions, but payments to Hashd al-Shaabi forces continue. The CENTCOM commander stated that some groups have stopped paying salaries and are sending funds to Tehran. Additionally, an explosion occurred at a Hashd al-Shaabi base in eastern Baghdad.

An earthquake was reported in the east of Tehran province on the morning of Sunday, October 18. The areas of Bumehen, Pardis, Rudehen, and Damavand experienced shaking. The event occurred around 4:00 to 4:12 AM.

Abbas Araghchi met with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaydi in Baghdad. The meeting focused on the Tehran-Washington agreement to stop the war and diplomatic efforts for regional security. Al-Zaydi emphasized resolving disputes through dialogue.

JD Vance, the US Vice President, said the US has achieved a decisive victory by destroying Iran's nuclear program. He emphasized that the war must continue to prevent the Islamic Republic from rebuilding its nuclear capabilities. Vance also stated that the presence of the US Navy in the Strait of Hormuz has maintained oil flow and prevented a sharp increase in fuel prices.

JD Vance, the US Vice President, defended the Trump administration's strategy regarding the war with Iran, stating that if the US leaves the region, gasoline prices will rise. He also said the US has achieved some victories and seeks Iran's commitment not to rebuild its nuclear program. Vance acknowledged mistakes in troop deployment and announced changes in military tactics to counter drones.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, stated that Washington agrees with the UK's assessment of the Islamic Republic's role in the attack plan on the Ferford base. The UK government accused the Revolutionary Guards of involvement in this plan. The Islamic Republic has denied these allegations.

Afrah Al-Zouba, Yemen's foreign minister, rejected Iran's proposal to mediate in the Yemen war. She accused Iran of supporting the Houthis and violating Yemen's sovereignty. Al-Zouba called on the international community to stop Iran's interventions and cut off financial resources to the Houthis.

A group of Iranians living in Washington gathered in front of the former embassy of the Islamic Republic. They commemorated the recent victims and those executed. They also protested the ongoing wave of executions in Iran.

Ahmad Nejatian, head of the Nursing Organization, stated that Iran faces a shortage of at least 100,000 nurses. The nurse-to-hospital-bed ratio in the country has reached one. This issue affects the quality of healthcare in Iran.

Farzin Karbasi stated that the Iraqi government lacks sufficient power to control armed groups close to the Islamic Republic. He warned that these groups could become active again if tensions escalate. These remarks refer to the security situation in Iraq.

Farzin Nadimi stated that extensive military attacks alone cannot prevent the reconstruction of Iran's nuclear program. He emphasized that as long as the technical knowledge and ability to manufacture centrifuge parts remain, complete destruction of the nuclear program is not assured.

Reuters reported that the Islamic Republic has helped increase the Houthis' military capabilities against Saudi Arabia by providing money, weapons, and training. The Revolutionary Guards and Hezbollah have transferred technical knowledge and training in missile and drone production to the Houthis. The Houthis have also used artificial intelligence to develop software and missile designs.

Mohammad Qaedi said the Islamic Republic simultaneously supports the Houthis militarily and intelligence-wise while presenting itself as a supporter of a political solution to the Yemen crisis. Tehran uses support for the Houthis as leverage and sends peace messages to Saudi Arabia. Mediation is one of Iran's foreign diplomacy tools.

Donald Trump announced that the military operation against the Islamic Republic is nearing its end and that gasoline prices will decrease after the war. JD Vance emphasized the decisive victory of the US and the continuation of operations to prevent the reconstruction of Iran's nuclear program. These statements were made in an interview with Kambiz Tavana.

The Russian Federal Security Service has arrested a Japanese journalist on charges of collecting military information for Japan's intelligence agency. This issue has increased tensions between Moscow and Tokyo. The charge has not yet been proven in court.

Ghassan Ashour said that the decrease in Iraq's oil revenues and the limitation of financial resources for armed groups could intensify conflicts among these groups. Part of the financial resources allocated to the Popular Mobilization Forces was given to commanders and senior politicians. Additionally, some of these resources were transferred through the Quds Force to groups close to the Islamic Republic in other countries.

Hossein Shariatmadari responded to Trump's remarks about the possible use of the 'mother of bombs' and stated that the Islamic Republic will respond to enemy attacks. He threatened that the infrastructure of the US and its allies will be targeted by Iranian missiles. Additionally, US military personnel and nuclear facilities of allied countries were declared targets by Iran.

The UK Maritime Trade Organization reported that two projectiles hit a tugboat near the port of Khorfakkan, UAE. The tugboat was damaged but continued its course. One person sustained minor injuries in the incident.

Ali Shirazi stated that no pressure tools have been able to deter the nation from confronting the US and Israel. He added that the enemy could not withstand the people's steadfastness. The Islamic Republic has also implemented a new system for managing shipping and energy transit in the Persian Gulf without US intervention.

Netanyahu said in an interview with Fox News that the Iranian people have become hostages of ideological thugs. He promised that if re-elected as Israel's prime minister, he would completely eliminate the threat from Iran. Netanyahu emphasized that the only way to address the current situation is to get rid of the Iranian regime.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated in the defense minister nominee's qualification session that Iran has not attacked any country in the past two centuries and does not intend to attack any. He emphasized that Iran will stand powerfully against any attack. The government also supports the nominee's plans to improve the living conditions of the armed forces.

Abbas Araghchi met with Ali Falih Al-Zaydi and Hakan Fidan in Baghdad. The discussions focused on stopping the war and preventing the spread of regional conflicts. Respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity of countries was also emphasized.

Amirparsa Eshkboos, 22 years old, was killed in Haft-Hoz, Tehran. His mother placed 9 apples to symbolize 9 months of pregnancy and separation from her son. The family found his body at Al-Ghadir Hospital.
Naser Hemmati, a citizen from Abdanan, was arrested to serve his prison sentence. He was transferred to the Mahpareh prison in Darreh Shahr. This event occurred yesterday.

Salar Velayatmadar stated that the Islamic Republic is fully prepared to face various enemy scenarios. He warned that if the US takes action, it will face a severe response. He also emphasized that people should be aware of the real dimensions of the global confrontation.

Mohsen Rezaei stated that the Islamic Republic's armed forces have prepared a more destructive plan than previous wars to counter new adventures. He said the threats from American and Israeli officials do not change the reality on the ground. Rezaei added that Tehran's new operational plan will not proceed according to known rules.

A man was arrested in Qods County on charges of assaulting a 33-year-old woman. He is accused of poisoning the woman with a drink to render her unconscious and then assaulting her. The incident was uncovered by police officers and the suspect was arrested.

An employee with 25 years of work experience complained about not receiving commodity baskets. A retiree with low income spoke about his family's financial difficulties. Additionally, the Imam Hussein loan fund in Kashmar is not returning people's money, and retirees have not received their salaries and benefits.

Hamidreza Hajibabaei, Vice-Speaker of Parliament, said that economic hardships and US pressures have strengthened the will of the Iranian nation, and the US is sinking deeper every day in the Persian Gulf quagmire. He added that the Iranian people are waiting for 'Al Trump' to drown in the turbulent sea of the Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf, and the Sea of Oman.

Ali Sadrazadeh said the simultaneous Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and rising tensions between the Islamic Republic, the US, and Israel have increased concerns. Qatar has warned about the Islamic Republic attacking civilian infrastructure. Tehran's financial and military support for the Houthis indicates a possible escalation of the regional crisis.
Arash Yazdani, 27 years old, was killed on the evening of January 8, 2026, in Haft-Hoz, Tehran. His sister blew out her birthday candle at his grave. This was done for Arash's lost dreams.

Today, Sunday, 26 Mehr, social security retirees held a protest gathering in Kermanshah. They demanded attention to their medical and livelihood problems. The gathering was held to express their demands.

Jalal Ejadi, a sociology professor, described the widespread protests in France as a reflection of public distrust in the government and economic difficulties. He noted the simultaneity of these protests with similar discontent in Italy. This has raised concerns about the spread of protest movements across Europe.

Donald Trump stated that the US military operation in the region will soon end and gasoline prices will decrease afterward. He said American forces have destroyed the nuclear capability of the Islamic Republic. Washington is also taking measures to prevent the reconstruction of this capability.
Mahshar Parandin, a Christian convert imprisoned in Evin, was granted medical leave. The leave lasts for 10 days and was issued with a pay slip. This event was reported on October 17, 2026.

Widespread protests continue in France and Italy in response to rising living costs and decreased purchasing power. Clashes between protesters and police have occurred, with some cities experiencing fires and looting. The French interior minister estimated about 550,000 participants in the marches.

Alireza Raeisi, a 21-year-old protester, was executed in Dastgerd prison in Isfahan. His eternal resting place is in the deserts of Anarak near the village of Eshin. His family was not informed of the exact burial location due to concerns about public gatherings.

Reports indicate a shortage of insulin in pharmacies and the black market. The cost of living, including food and education, has increased significantly. There are also issues with renewing residency cards involving high fees.

The head of the Iranian Psychiatric Association reported a widespread shortage of psychiatric drugs in the country. Both imported and domestically produced drugs such as venlafaxine and sertraline have become scarce. These shortages have forced patients to change or stop treatment, increasing the risk of disease relapse.

Abbas Moqtadaei stated that countries hosting Americans and Israelis in the region are not qualified to comment on regional security unless they compensate for the damages caused. He added that Saudi Arabia should return to the path emphasized by the Quran and avoid discord among Muslims. Moqtadaei also emphasized that Saudi Arabia has made mistakes trusting the US and Israel and needs to reconsider.

Mehdi Maskinnavaz, a political prisoner in Lakaan prison in Rasht, has been deprived of proper medical treatment despite needing knee surgery and suffering from skin burns. His treatment has been halted for over two years, and prison officials have classified his condition as non-emergency. He suffers from severe back disc and knee pain and has not been transferred to an outside hospital.

Setareh Ghorbani explained the educational problems in France, including budget cuts, teacher shortages, and increased class sizes. She said these issues are linked to the economic situation of families. She also emphasized that unequal access to educational facilities contradicts the principle of equality.

Ahmad Nadari, a member of the parliament's presidium, reported attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait in recent months and said the UAE is different. He called for stronger actions to break the naval and air blockade. Nadari also mentioned the closure of Najaf airport and the insecurity of regional airports.

A group of retirees in Rasht gathered on Sunday, October 18, to protest economic difficulties. They chanted slogans demanding the cancellation of death sentences. This gathering was reported based on videos received by Iran International.
Kosar Eftekhari was injured in her eye during the 2022 protests. She continued her political and human rights activities afterward. A special interview with her was conducted by Ali Hasanpour.

The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson confirmed the closure of all border crossings between Iran and Pakistan. The naval blockade has halted Iran's maritime trade. Iranian officials have turned to land borders to compensate for this situation.

The Ministry of Science has cut ties with Farzad Kolbali, an adjunct lecturer at the University of Tehran. His classes have been canceled and he is banned from entering the university. This decision was made due to his publication of offensive content on social media.

During the first six months of the current year, 13 workers died in Khorasan Razavi province. These incidents occurred due to lack of workplace safety and poor working conditions. This statistic was reported by Harana News Agency.

The Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that Hamas demands 10,000 shekels from Gaza merchants for each truck and threatens those who refuse to pay. The son of one merchant has been detained, and merchants have stopped coordinating truck entries out of fear. Hamas disrupts the supply of goods in Gaza to finance its operations.

The head of Tehran's City Council's Urban Development Commission announced that over 60% of the capital's taxis are worn out and have reached the end of their useful life. These taxis face issues such as low safety, high pollution, and poor service quality. Additionally, the increase in car prices and drivers' livelihood problems were highlighted.

Ahmad Nadri stated that the Islamic Republic has targeted Bahrain and Kuwait in recent months, but the UAE is exempt from this rule. He called for stronger action against the UAE and warned that Iran's maritime and air blockade may continue and a land blockade might begin. Nadri also said that after Iran's airspace was closed, UAE flights to various global destinations should not continue.

Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social about the unrest in France, saying borders should be closed and control regained. He stated that France is burning and migration of hateful people has destroyed the country.
Saro Sadeghzadeh, a 17-year-old teenager from Baneh, was arrested by intelligence officers. He was transferred to a security detention center in Sanandaj. This event occurred yesterday.

Mohammad Reza Naqdi, senior advisor to the commander of the IRGC, stated during the Jan Fadaian exercise that the missile capabilities of the armed forces threaten all enemy assets in the region. He added that in case of a miscalculation, the infrastructure and investments of the aggressors would be within operational range. Their security would be directly endangered.
Sina Parvizi, a citizen of Kamyaran, was summoned to the intelligence office and after several hours of interrogation, he was released on bail.

A group of Iranians residing in Sweden held a protest in Malmö on Sunday, October 18. The protest was against executions by the Islamic Republic. A video of this gathering was received by Iran International.

Ata Hosseinian spoke about the continued gasoline queues in some provinces and Masoud Pezeshkian's remarks about no need for gasoline imports. He said that consumption management is actually suppressing demand and limiting people's access to fuel. He also doubts that the financial savings will be used to improve people's livelihoods.

Farzad Kolbali, an adjunct professor at the University of Tehran's Faculty of Law, has been banned from teaching and entering the university. The Basij of the Faculty of Law claims this ban was enforced through their efforts. Kolbali had previously faced criticism from media and security institutions due to his statements.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that two unidentified projectiles hit a tugboat near the coast of the United Arab Emirates. The incident occurred on Sunday, October 18, 2026. No further details have been provided.

Tesla unveiled flying car technology, which received mixed reactions in Iran. Some technology enthusiasts welcomed the event, while some government media downplayed it. This issue has reignited discussions about Iran's gap with global technological developments.

Iran's foreign minister announced that Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days remains valid. Iran has presented a seven-point plan to the US and is awaiting Washington's response. If Tehran's conditions are accepted, the Strait will reopen on the sixth day and negotiations will begin on the seventh.

Since last year, salaries of employees and workers have increased by 20%, while essential goods prices have risen over 400%. In some areas like Chabahar, stores refuse to provide goods due to unpaid government debts. Issues such as lack of cooling systems in schools and unpaid contractor workers' wages have also been reported.

A group of Iranians living in the UK held the campaign "9 Apples, 9 Months of Separation" on Saturday, October 17. The campaign supports seeking justice for mothers. They commemorated the memory of the martyrs of the national revolution.

The head of Bushehr University of Medical Sciences reported a shortage of about 700 nursing staff in the province. Nurses' salaries in some southern areas are less than 40 million tomans. This situation has reduced graduates' interest in employment and made it difficult to recruit nursing staff.

Arash Azarmi, a member of Iran International's editorial team, responded to the former labor minister's remarks denying an economic disaster in Iran. He described the Islamic Republic as an occupying sect characterized by foolishness, plunder, and crime. Azarmi also stated that various political powers are holding the country's economic resources hostage and plundering them.

Hamidreza Hajibabaei, the deputy speaker of the parliament, stated that if the US brings 'mother bombs,' the Islamic Republic will respond with 'father missiles.' He said they have plans to counter all types of US bombs. He also accused the US of choosing to shout slogans instead of taking action against the Islamic Republic's armed forces.

Omid Shabani explained the differences between protests in Iran and France in an interview with Iran International. He said that in Iran protesters face execution, while in France police are not allowed to use live ammunition. Iranians in Paris continue to support the people of Iran.

On the evening of Saturday, October 17, protest leaflets were posted throughout the city of Zanjan. The leaflets read: "The Islamic Republic is collapsing, the end of the dark night is bright." This video was released by Iran International.

The Football League Organization has announced that men are prohibited from attending women's football matches. This restriction includes spectators, journalists, photographers, cameramen, and male club managers. The decision was issued by higher authorities and the league organization is obliged to implement it.

Tractor players left the field after racist chants from fans at Sirous Ghayeghran Stadium in Anzali, and the match was not held. Negotiations between coaches and officials were unsuccessful. The club owner stated that if the match is forfeited 3-0 against Tractor, they will withdraw from the Premier League.

Sharif Ashnab, a citizen from Malekshahi, remains in detention in Ilam prison after 19 days without a clear status. His situation has not changed during this period. This issue was reported by Harana News Agency.

Ahmad Nadari, a member of the parliament's presidium, called for building an atomic bomb and revising the fatwa on nuclear weapons. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic should move towards establishing ultimate military deterrence. Nadari stated that this issue has been raised and supported for over a decade.
